chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafith al-Baghdadi narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih narrated to us, who said: Shu'ayb ibn Rashid narrated to us from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) stood to address the people at Siffin on a Friday — five days before the battle of al-Harir — and said: Praise be to God for His surpassing blessings upon all His creation, the righteous and the wicked alike, and for His conclusive proofs over His creation — those who disobeyed Him and those who obeyed Him alike.

If He pardons, it is out of His grace; if He punishes, it is for what their own hands have sent forth — and God is never unjust to His servants. I praise Him for His gracious trials and for the abundance of His blessings, and I seek His help in the religious matters that have befallen us. I believe in Him and I rely on Him — sufficient is God as a guardian.

Then indeed I testify that there is no god but God, alone without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with guidance and His religion which He approved of. He was worthy of it and He chose him above all the servants to convey His message and His proofs over His creation — and He was, as He knew him to be, gentle and merciful. He was the most noble of God's creation in lineage, the most beautiful of them in appearance, the most valiant of them in spirit, the most dutiful of them to his parent, and the most trustworthy of them in covenant.

Never did a Muslim or a disbeliever attach to him any complaint of injustice at all. Rather, he would be wronged, yet he would forgive; he would have power, yet he would pardon and overlook; until he passed away in obedience to God, patient over what afflicted him, striving for God as He ought to be striven for, worshiping God until certainty (death) came to him. His departure (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) was the greatest calamity for all the people of the earth — the righteous and the wicked alike. Then he left among you the Book of God, which commands you to obey God and forbids you from disobeying Him.

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) entrusted me with a covenant that I will never depart from. Your enemy has come before you, and you have recognized who their leader is — he calls them to falsehood — while the cousin of your Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) is in your midst calling you to obedience of your Lord and to act according to the Sunnah of your Prophet. Not equal is the one who prayed before every male — none preceded me in prayer except the Prophet of God. I am, by God, among the people of Badr. By God, you are surely upon truth and the people are surely upon falsehood.

Do not let the people be more patient in their falsehood — gathering upon it — than you in your truth, from which you disperse. Fight them, and God will punish them by your hands. If you do not, God will punish them by the hands of others. His companions responded to him and said: O Commander of the Faithful! Rise against the people whenever you wish — by God, we seek no substitute for you; we die with you and we live. So he said to them, scanning them: By He in Whose hand is my soul! The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) once looked at me as I was striking before him with my sword, and he said: 'There is no sword but Dhulfiqar, and there is no youth but Ali.' Then he said to me: 'O Ali, you are to me as Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me — and your life, O Ali, and your death are with me.'

By God, I have not lied, nor been called a liar; I have not gone astray, nor led others astray; and I have not forgotten what was entrusted to me — for then I would indeed be forgetful. I am upon a clear proof from my Lord which He made plain to His Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), who in turn made it plain to me. I am upon the manifest path, and I follow it precisely. Then he rose against the people on Thursday, and they fought from the time the sun rose until the twilight faded. The people's prayer that day was nothing but the takbir at the times of prayer. Ali (peace be upon him) killed on that day, with his own hand, five hundred and six individuals from among that group of people. So the people of the Levant began calling: O Ali! Fear God regarding those who remain! And they raised their copies of the Quran upon the tips of their spears.

key_terms.المصاحف على أطراف القنا: The raising of the Quran on spear-tips — the stratagem used by Mu'awiyah's forces to call for arbitration and halt the battle at Siffin
key_terms.الهرير: al-Harir — the intense 'rumbling' phase of the Battle of Siffin in 37 AH, named for the sound of combat
key_terms.ذو الفقار: Dhulfiqar — the famous sword of the Prophet given to Imam Ali, whose name means 'the one with notches'
key_terms.منزلة هارون من موسى: The hadith of Manzila — the Prophet's declaration that Ali's relation to him is as Harun's to Musa, except there is no prophet after him

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say in his sermon at the Battle of Siffin?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates Imam Ali's famous Friday sermon at the Battle of Siffin, five days before the intense phase of fighting known as al-Harir. Transmitted by Imam al-Baqir, the sermon opens with a profound praise of God and testimony of faith, followed by an eloquent eulogy of the Prophet Muhammad's noble character, the covenant Ali received from him, and a call to arms against those who had gathered under Mu'awiyah's banner of falsehood. The hadith concludes with the account of the battle itself — Ali's extraordinary valor in killing 506 enemies single-handedly — and the famous ruse of the Syrians raising the Quran on spear-tips to halt the fighting, a pivotal moment in Islamic history.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Umar al-Hafith al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. `Abd al-`Aziz b. al-Ja`d narrated to us. He said: `Abd al-Rahman b. Salih narrated to us. He said: Shu`ayb b. Rashid narrated to us from Jabir from Abi Ja`far (as). He said:

`Ali (as) delivered a sermon to the people at Siffin on Friday, five days before the battle. So, he said: Praise be to Allah for His great blessings which He bestowed upon all His creation, the righteous and the wretched alike; and for His elaborate proofs over His creation, those who disobey Him and those who obey Him alike.

Surely, if He forgives, then that is a bounty from Him, and if He punishes, then that is what proceeded from their own hands – and Allah is not oppressive to the servants. I praise Him for resolving hardships, manifesting blessings, and His help in fulfilling the orders of our religion. I believe in Him and I rely on Him, as Allah is sufficient as a guardian.

Then, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, one without partners, and that Muhammad is His Servant and His Messenger. He sent him with guidance and His religion which He is pleased with, and he was of its nature. He chose him over all the servants to preach His message and His proofs over His creation – and He was gentle and merciful with him. He was the most honoured of Allah’s creation, the most beautiful of them in appearance, the most valiant of them in spirit, the best of them to his parent, the most secure of them in agreements

– no Muslim nor disbeliever ever claimed to have been wronged by him. Rather, he would be wronged, and he would forgive and pardon; until he passed away in obedience to Allah, patient over what afflicted him, striving for Allah as He ought to be strived for, worshiping Allah until certainty (death) came to him. His (s) leave of us was the greatest calamity for all the people of the world, the righteous and the wretched alike. He left the Book of Allah among you, which commands you to obey Allah and prohibits you from disobeying Him.

The Messenger of Allah (s) gave me a covenant that I will not leave. Your enemies have come to you, and you have recognized who their leader is – he calls them to falsehood – and the cousin of your Prophet (s) is in your midst calling you to the obedience of your Lord and fulfilling the sunna of your Prophet. There is no equal to the one who prayed before every male. None preceded me in prayer except the Prophet of Allah. I am, by Allah, from the people of Badr. By Allah, you are surely upon truth, and the people are surely upon falsehood.

We cannot bear their falsehood patiently as they gather to it and split away from their truth. Fight them, and Allah will punish them with your hands. If you do not do that, then Allah will punish them with the hands of others. So, his companions responded to him, and they said: O Amir al-Mu’minin! Go forth to the people if you wish, for by Allah, we live and we die with you. So, he said to them: By He in whose hand is my soul! The Messenger of Allah (s) looked at me while I was striking before him with my sword, then he said: “There is no sword except the dhulfiqar, and there is no youth except `Ali.” Then, he said to me: “O `Ali! You are to me as Harun was to Musa, except there is no prophet after me – by your life, O `Ali, and by your death.”

I have never lied, nor have I misled, nor have I forgotten what was entrusted to me. Surely, I am upon a proof from my Lord that he had given to His Prophet (s), and he had given it to me. Surely, I am upon the clear path, and I go quickly upon it. Then, he went forth to the people on Thursday, and they fought from sunrise to sunset. Those people (the enemy) did not pray on that day except for reciting the takbir during the timings of the prayers. That day, `Ali (as) killed five hundred and six individuals from that group of people with his hands. So, the next morning, the people of the Levant called: O `Ali! Fear Allah regarding those who remain. So, they raised the codices [of the Quran] from the tips of their spears.
